description: The New Earth Project Pilot: Climate Change Mitigation Through Food Waste Reduction is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Recognizing the climate change mitigation potential that Johnson-Su bioreactors hold, the Upper Gila Watershed Alliance (UGWA) founded the New Earth Project, currently based in Santa Clara, New Mexico. The New Earth Project is a climate solutions program that addresses interconnected environmental issues including carbon draw-down, food system resilience, food waste reduction, and soil improvement. Coverage: Santa Clara, New Mexico (2024). The toolkit gives Santa Clara, New Mexico as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
